To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we identified LeFLS2 in tomato as the receptor kinase mediating the perception of bacterial flagellin.
we identified LeFLS2 (a tomato flagellin perception gene) by using flg15Ecoli (an elicitor derived from E. coli) and that LeFLS2 represents the flagellin perception receptor of tomato.

we have made use of the fact that tomato is more responsive to flagellins from E.coli than A.thaliana to identify the flagellin receptors in both plant species, and that we have identified LeFLS2 in tomato, a functional, species-specific flagellin receptor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification, molecular characterization and functional analysis of the tomato flagella receptor LeFLS1, an orthologue to the Arabidopsis receptor AtFLS2.
the molecular identification and characterization of a flagellin receptor (LeFLS2) in tomato, which is the first such protein to be described in the Solanaceae family.
the molecular identification of the flagellin recognition receptor in tomato.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
LeFLS2 exhibits characteristically different perception specificity to AtFLS and NtFLS, and that the LeFLS receptor is not able to recognize the Arabidopsis flagellin peptide flg22.
LeFLS2 represents the flagellin-receptor of tomato.
LeFLS2 represents the functional tomato homologue of AtFLS2 and that the flg22/FLS2 system in Arabidopsis is not conserved in the Solanaceae.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified the first flagellin receptor from Solanaceae family and characterized its perception specificities.
we have identified the flagellin receptors in tomato and Arabidopsis, which are orthologous to each other.
we have identified LeFLS2 and characterized it as a functional flagellin receptor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
LeFLS2 represents a functional, specific receptor for flagellin in tomato, and that the flg15Ecoli epitope of flagellin can serve as a specific elicitor in tomato.
